title: Pothos: the forgiving houseplant
text:
Pothos is one of the most forgiving houseplants for beginners.
It tolerates low light, but variegated leaves keep their yellow or white patterns best in bright, indirect light.
Allow the top half of the soil to dry out between waterings. Drooping leaves are usually a sign the plant needs water.
Pothos can be propagated in a glass of water: cut a stem just below a node, and roots usually appear within 2 to 4 weeks.
Its leaves are toxic to cats and dogs if chewed, so keep it out of reach of pets.
Trailing stems can grow more than 2 meters long indoors; trimming them encourages fuller growth near the pot.
